Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Town, shops & places

community noun

the people of a place

also local community, neighbourhood, neighborhood

classical

Cato Agr. 4
Cic. Verr. 2.4.96: nōtum vīcīnitātī (Lewis & Short)

vīcīnitās, vīcīnitātis f.

noun, third declension

the neighbourhood: the people who live round about

Lewis & Short: neighbourhood, i.e. neighbours. The local community, on which Cato’s farmer depends.

Other words

  • cīvitās, cīvitātis f. — a community of citizens; a town and its people

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 178, 294

    The community as a political body (see state, a country).

  • commūnitās, commūnitātis f. — fellowship, a sense of community

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.157: commūnitās et conjūnctiō hūmāna (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero’s word for what people share, not for a group of people.

  • conventus, conventūs m. — the body of Roman citizens living in a provincial town

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Caes. BC 2.19 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Lig. 24 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: persons associated in a provincial town for the sake of trade; the classical model for a community abroad.

  • vīcīnia, vīcīniae f. — neighbourhood, vicinity

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 2.3.27: proximae vīcīniae habitat (Lewis & Short); Traupman 350

    Lewis & Short: mostly poetic and post-Augustan; prose prefers vīcīnitās.

Examples

  • sī tē libenter vīcīnitās vidēbit, facilius tua vēndēs, opera facilius locābis, operāriōs facilius condūcēs

    if the neighbourhood is glad to see you, you will sell your produce more easily, let out work more easily, hire labourers more easilyCato Agr. 4

See also neighbour, village, town, state.
